thread.title: Google sold at least $2.7 billion worth of hardware during the holidays

author: Max A. Cherney
title: Google sold at least $2.7 billion worth of hardware during the holidays
text:
Alphabet Inc.-owned Google pocketed at least $2.7 billion from hardware sales during the fourth quarter, the company said late Thursday.
Buried in the company’s financial results largely revolving around the search giant’s $27.23 billion advertising business lies the revenue known as Google Other, which banked $4.69 billion. Of that, its cloud division made $1 billion , and the Play Store arm earned less than $1 billion — leaving at least $2.7 billion in hardware sales left over.
While cloud was the largest contributor in the third quarter, and remains a fast-growing segment, Google’s new lineup of hardware, announced in October, likely made a significant contribution — especially with the seasonal boost from holiday sales, Alphabet Chief Financial Officer Ruth Porat hinted at on the third-quarter conference call with analysts. 
Among the new gadgets on sale for the holiday quarter that Google launched: its new Pixel 2 smartphones, a virtual-reality accessory for the phones, wireless ear buds, as well as a range of new smart speakers. The most inexpensive speaker, the Google Home Mini, aggressively marketed and priced at a discount for much of the holiday season at $30, was the easiest way for consumers to access the company’s virtual assistant.
Jackdaw Research analyst Jan Dawson has told MarketWatch in the past that he expects the Home Mini to be Google’s mass-market product. “It’s one of the only ones that may show up in financial results,” he said.

While the new products aren’t flawless — a bug on the Mini forced the company to make changes — and reviews not always perfect , $2.7 billion in quarterly sales is nothing to sneeze at. But it’s still dwarfed by rival Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.21% and its $61 billion in quarterly iPhone revenue, or 77.3 million units .
No word yet on what financial analysts will do with the new-found knowledge and how it will figure into their forecasts for the next quarter. At the moment, analysts polled by FactSet model $4.09 billion in first-quarter sales and $5.83 billion in this year’s December quarter for the Other unit.
Alphabet class A stock GOOGL, -0.05% GOOG, -0.19% was down 2.5% in late trading. The class A stock has gained 45% in the past 12 months, with the S&P 500 index SPX, -0.06% rising 24%.
